# GAN comparative study: super-resolution for low-resolution video

*Generated by `python -m islvit.gan_report` from `runs/gan_study/`. Every number below is read from a result file.*

## What the GAN does, and where

Every clip reaches the hand detector through `islvit/data/crops.py::read_sampled_frames`. Video below the 720p working height is upscaled there before MediaPipe looks for hands. Until now that upscale was bicubic. The GAN (`islvit/sr/`) replaces that one interpolation when `--sr` is passed. Native 1080p INCLUDE never takes this branch, so the shipped model's clean result cannot change.

```
video -> decode -> [below 720p?  bicubic  |  SR-GAN x4 -> area to 720p] -> MediaPipe -> crops + landmarks -> ISL-ViT-Tiny
```

| Model | Stage | Starts from | Generator params | Discriminator params | Iterations | Peak LR | Perceptual features | Minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `runs/sr_l1` | l1 | scratch | 621,424 | — | 100,000 | 0.0002 | — | 55.6 |
| `runs/sr_gan_v1` | gan | `runs/sr_l1/generator.pt` | 621,424 | 4376897 | 60,000 | 0.0001 | vgg19 | 236.8 |
| `runs/sr_gan` | gan | `runs/sr_gan_v1/generator.pt` | 621,424 | 4376897 | 80,000 | 5e-05 | vgg19 | 261.4 |

Generator: a compact Real-ESRGAN-style network (SRVGG). Discriminator: U-Net with spectral normalisation. Losses: L1, then L1 + perceptual + 0.1 × adversarial. It is trained only on INCLUDE training-session clips (`islvit/sr/patches.py` asserts none of the 472 test clips or held-out sessions are used). Both stages keep the final EMA weights after a fixed number of iterations, with no checkpoint selection.

**Two GANs.** The study was first run with SR-GAN v1 (`runs/sr_gan_v1`: 60,000 GAN iterations from SR-L1). SR-GAN v2 (`runs/sr_gan`), which every 'SR-GAN' column below refers to, continues from the v1 generator with a fresh discriminator at half the peak learning rate, so its generator has had 140,000 adversarial iterations in all. v2 was trained **after** v1's results were known, to get the strongest GAN that fitted the remaining time, so it is not part of the pre-registered design. The v1 results are reported in full under *SR-GAN v1 against v2*, so nothing is hidden by the swap. SR-L1, the no-GAN control, is unchanged.

## Study design

- **Inputs:** the same 472 held-out clips behind the 85.9 % headline (`splits/_test472_paths.csv`), degraded inside the frame reader before detection: 360p + JPEG 60, 240p + JPEG 50, 180p + JPEG 40.
- **Arms:** bicubic (the current pipeline, no GAN), SR-L1 (the same generator trained without the adversarial loss, which isolates what the GAN adds), and SR-GAN.
- **Models:** the three shipped INT4 models, frozen; the same three in FP32; and the FP32 models fine-tuned for 150 epochs on 360p training video through each front end (bicubic or SR-GAN).
- **Metric:** masked-50 six-view TTA top-1, mean ± sd over three seeds.
- **Pre-registered rule:** a front end *helps* only if the mean top-1 rises, all three seeds move the same way, and the pooled exact McNemar p < 0.05. *The GAN helps* only if SR-GAN beats SR-L1 by that rule; otherwise any gain belongs to learned super-resolution, not to the adversarial training.

## Detection and hallucination

Share of hand frames with a genuine detection, and agreement with the clean 1080p extraction of the same clips. *Extra hands* are found in the degraded video but not in the clean one. *Misplaced* hands are found in both but more than 5 % of the frame height apart. A GAN that raises detection by inventing hands would show up here.

| Input | Arm | Left hand | Right hand | Face | Presence agreement | Extra hands | Missed hands | Wrist error, median | Misplaced |

## Image quality on held-out patches

1200 patches from held-out sessions, at 720p working resolution (median sharpness of the originals: 73). PSNR and SSIM reward smooth averages, so the PSNR-trained SR-L1 is expected to score higher than the GAN on them; sharpness is variance of the Laplacian, the measure behind the report's 'CISLR crops are 2.1× blurrier' finding (§11.5).

| Input | Arm | PSNR (dB) | SSIM | Sharpness | ms / patch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L1 360p | Bicubic (no GAN) | 34.51 | 0.940 | 24 | — |
| L1 360p | SR-L1 (no adversarial loss) | 35.16 | 0.953 | 60 | 1.657 |
| L1 360p | SR-GAN | 34.40 | 0.942 | 71 | 1.488 |
| L1 360p | SR-GAN v1 | 34.49 | 0.942 | 70 | 1.487 |
| L2 240p | Bicubic (no GAN) | 31.97 | 0.893 | 8 | — |
| L2 240p | SR-L1 (no adversarial loss) | 33.66 | 0.925 | 23 | 1.117 |
| L2 240p | SR-GAN | 32.79 | 0.912 | 34 | 0.897 |
| L2 240p | SR-GAN v1 | 32.69 | 0.911 | 34 | 0.877 |
| L3 180p | Bicubic (no GAN) | 30.07 | 0.856 | 4 | — |
| L3 180p | SR-L1 (no adversarial loss) | 31.83 | 0.900 | 16 | 1.021 |
| L3 180p | SR-GAN | 31.09 | 0.884 | 32 | 0.828 |
| L3 180p | SR-GAN v1 | 31.07 | 0.883 | 31 | 0.806 |

## Reproduce

```bash
bash run_gan_study.sh          # resume-safe; about a day on one RTX 3060 (bicubic, SR-L1, SR-GAN v1)
GAN_ITERS=80000 bash run_gan_study_v2.sh   # SR-GAN v2 and everything that depends on it
python -m islvit.gan_report    # this document and figures 21-23
```
